# Connecting the Dots: Reader Ratings, Bibliographic Data, and Machine-Learning Algorithms for Monograph Selection

[Jingshan Xiao](https://www.tandfonline.com/author/Xiao%2C+Jingshan) Presenters View further author information & [Wenli Gao](https://www.tandfonline.com/author/Gao%2C+Wenli) Presenters

...

Recommender systems “analyze user profiles, content items, and the connections between them, and try to predict future user behavior.”

...

While the _New York Times_ publishes best seller titles based on the rates of sales, they do not have any connection to user ratings. By leveraging data from Goodreads, the world’s largest site for readers and book recommendations, this project builds a simple recommender system that produces _New York Times_ best seller titles that have higher user ratings using a Bayes estimator. Another part of the project was to build a recommender system that had the ability to refer selectors to books that were similar to a particular title. Drawing on bibliographic data from highly rated items, the recommender system suggests items with similar features using similarity metrics.
